Hypothesis: Static ML trained on nominal telemetry fails under operational and sensor distribution shifts.
Empirical Metric Evidence: Within flexpulse_final_test_v5, Static RF achieves ID F1=0.7477 (Event Recall=76.0%) and OOD F1=0.6975 (Event Recall=76.56%), missing 23.44% of OOD events. Fixed threshold collapses to Specificity=0.2984.
Statistical Significance: Yes (Event Miss Rate = 23.44%, Fixed Baseline Collapses to Spec = 0.2984)
Defensible Scientific Conclusion: Supported: Static ML avoids fixed-threshold collapse but exhibits inadequate fault sensitivity, missing 23.44% of events under OOD shifts.

Hypothesis: A 5.0 s initial reference calibration interval restores detection performance without continuous tracking.
Empirical Metric Evidence: Initial calibration (M3) achieves Event Recall=92.19% and Balanced Acc to 0.9028, but increased false alarms yield OOD F1=0.7633 (Delta F1 = +0.0595 vs M2, 95% CI [-0.0648, 0.1596], p = 0.3220).
Statistical Significance: No significant F1 change (p = 0.3220, 95% CI [-0.0648, 0.1596]); Event Recall Delta = +15.63%
Defensible Scientific Conclusion: Supported for sensitivity, not F1: Initial calibration recovers missed fault events, but increases false alarms without temporal filtering.

Hypothesis: Continuous confidence-gated adaptive calibration provides significant performance improvement over initial calibration.
Empirical Metric Evidence: Adaptive ML (M4) matches Initial Calibration (M3) identically: Delta F1 = 0.0000 (95% CI [0.0000, 0.0000], empirical p = 1.0000).
Defensible Scientific Conclusion: Refuted: Online adaptation provides zero incremental detection gain over initial reference calibration under tested USB-C fault dynamics.

Hypothesis: Multi-stage confidence and stability gating prevents tracker contamination during slow creeping faults.
Empirical Metric Evidence: Defensive confidence and stability gates eliminate creeping fault absorption: contamination drops from 2.11% (ungated) to 0.0% (M4/A3).
Defensible Scientific Conclusion: Supported: Defensive safety gates completely shield the baseline from adapting into genuine gradual fault resistance increases.

Hypothesis: Causal multi-window persistence filtering suppresses transient false alarms at an acceptable detection latency cost.
Empirical Metric Evidence: Persistence N=2 cuts false alarm events by 38.83% (515 to 315) and raises F1 to 0.8559 (Delta F1 = +0.0932, p < 0.01) at +0.2085 s added latency; Event Recall is 92.19%.
Defensible Scientific Conclusion: Supported: N=2 represents an intentional engineering trade-off cutting false alarms by 38.83% at +0.2085 s latency while preserving 92.19% event recall.
